page: Microsoft Azure D96ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. System memory totals 384.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A bundled 5670 GB local NVMe SSD provides high-speed ephemeral scratch space, while accelerated cryptographic and vector instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and VAES are supported directly on the CPU.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution capabilities across both single-threaded and distributed multi-core workloads. The AMD EPYC cores deliver top-decile performance in stress-ng compute evaluations and PassMark CPU metrics, achieving an overall PassMark CPU score of 117050.24. Memory throughput reaches 311.62 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 174.65 GB/sec for uncached writes, complementing strong multi-threaded compression metrics such as 610.83 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Key-value operations also show exceptional speed, logging 140.26 million operations per second in Redis SET testing.

Qualitatively, the D96ads_v7 presents high resource density by packing 96 compute threads, substantial memory, and multi-terabyte local NVMe storage onto a single virtual node. The lack of discrete GPUs limits its application for high-throughput AI training, though its AVX-512 instruction support delivers respectable CPU-based inference throughput on small and medium models. With its combination of raw processor throughput, integrated low-latency local storage, and balanced memory capacity, the instance is well suited for enterprise database clusters, distributed caching systems, ETL data pipelines, large-scale CI/CD build environments, and web serving fleets.
description: Microsoft Azure D96ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 96 dedicated vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. It includes 384.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM general-purpose ratio, and comes integrated with 5670 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage. Lacking discrete GPUs, it relies on x86_64 vector extensions such as AVX-512 and VAES for hardware acceleration. In benchmark evaluations, the instance ranks in the top tier for multi-core stress testing, PassMark CPU computation, and in-memory key-value processing, recording 140.26 million Redis SET operations per second. Its massive core density and local NVMe storage deliver strong qualitative efficiency for high-demand enterprise software, making it an effective choice for relational databases, Redis caching layers, heavy compilation jobs, ETL processing, and large-scale web application infrastructure.
